text: Team guide · 30 September 2026
textPreview: Team guide · 30 September 2026

text:
Today we will choose between three ways of working with AI. Dot is useful when you want follow-through over time. A repeated check and a focused task are different needs. This presentation uses the built-in Claude Code command; a custom loop may behave differently.
Sources: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks; https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/codex/using_goals_in_codex
Official artwork: https://learn.chatgpt.com/images/codex/dots/default-dot.svg

text:
Think of an assistant who remembers the assignment and follows up between conversations. Dot can research, work with documents and data, and help build software. It can finish an individual task even while a broader responsibility continues. Availability is rolling out and depends on account and workspace access.

text: “Has a test” versus “uses judgment” does not separate Dot from /loop.
textPreview: “Has a test” versus “uses judgment” does not separate Dot from /loop.

text:
The original verifier idea describes a custom repair loop: attempt, test, fix, repeat. It is useful, but it is not the definition of Claude Code’s built-in /loop. In current Claude Code, omitting an interval can let Claude choose the delay. Both approaches involve model judgment. Dot can use objective checks too.

text:
These are recommended defaults, not exclusive capabilities. A normal Codex task can investigate, edit and test within one request. Dot adds coordination and follow-up across work. For a difficult task with a measurable finish line, Codex Goals are another option.

text:
Ask the room to choose: “Summarize this document” → normal chat. “Check the build while I work” → /loop. “Keep next week’s client demo on track” → Dot. These recommendations are based on scope and follow-up, not whether a result is subjective. For fixed-interval /loop, ask Claude to cancel the job when finished; recurring jobs expire after seven days in current docs. Re-check product documentation before reusing this deck after feature changes.
